what_was_fetched: Full text PDF from MDPI's open-access file host (mdpi-res.com), pdftotext -layout: item1-urbansci-10-612-elisha-arbel-aiche-portnov.txt (19 pp.; footer 'Urban Sci. 2026, 10, 612  N of 19' marks pages). Crossref metadata and abstract: item1-crossref-metadata.json (CC BY 4.0, published 2026-10-22). The www.mdpi.com HTML and /pdf routes returned an access-denied page to ordinary requests; nothing paywalled was involved (the paper is open access).
verdict: ENRICH concepts/tax-capitalization.md (short passage). Not a NEW page: the paper is about an area-based tax on floor area, not land value; its tax-on-price coefficient is small and cross-sectional; and the main text has internal inconsistencies (see uncertainties). Insertion point: section '## Limits and Caveats', as a new bullet placed after the paragraph that ends '...see [Falkenbach et al. (2026)](/wiki/falkenbach-helsinki-land-lease-information-capitalization/).' and before the bullet beginning '- **Timing neutrality is contested at the margin:**'. Suggested content (impersonal, no process narration): an area-based tax shows cost-view capitalization without tracking value. Israel's Arnona is charged per square metre at a zone tariff on the occupant, with tariff ranges approved by the Interior Ministry and zone boundaries set by the municipality, so it does not adjust automatically when prices move. In a 2026 hedonic study of 5,108 Haifa sales (2020-2025) a higher per-square-metre tariff is associated with lower prices, and tariffs are lower where SO2 is higher, which the authors read as a partial compensation that does not offset the pollution price penalty. State that this is evidence on a floor-area tax, not on land or site-value taxation, and that the study is one city and cross-sectional. Add a Sources entry annotated 'used for ...' with grade B (MDPI venue noted in Sources only). ENRICH, so no inbound-link requirement. Cross-link to a future research page only once the BACKLOG [SOURCE-BLOCKED] Dai & Felsenstein lead is built.
claim_grade: B (empirical, peer-reviewed). Source tier per EDITORIAL 4c: Tier 1 by rubric (Boris Portnov, University of Haifa School of Environmental Studies, established urban-economics scholar with a peer-reviewed record on Israeli housing and property taxation; co-authors are academic economists at Western Galilee College); not listed in sources/audit/people-tiers.json. Cap at B and restrict the wiki to what the tables report: the abstract's '2SLS' framing is not matched by any reported 2SLS table and the paper's own Durbin-Wu-Hausman test supports OLS/SEM (see uncertainties).

uncertainties: The abstract says '2SLS' and 'PM10 displays a positive association with tax rates', but the main text reports no 2SLS second-stage table; Sec. 6.5 says the Durbin-Wu-Hausman test fails to reject exogeneity and the OLS and SEM estimates are the ones reported. Table 4 (tax equation) retains only SO2; NOX and PM10 tax-equation coefficients are not tabulated. T1 should not repeat the abstract's NOX-negative / PM10-positive tax-rate claims as tabulated results.

The conclusion says 'municipal taxation is positively capitalized into housing values' (Sec. 8) while Table 3 gives a negative Arnona coefficient and Sec. 6.2 says higher tax goes with lower values; read as 'capitalized as a cost'. The wording is the paper's own and is unreliable.

Arnona is 96 per cent correlated with apartment size and rises stepwise with size, so the tax coefficient may largely proxy size; the effect is small (T0 arithmetic, not in the paper: 25.58 SD x 3.98e-5 is about 0.1 per cent of price per SD of Arnona).
The unit of the tariff (NIS per m2 per year or per month) is not stated; do not restate it as an annual burden.

Table 2 has implausible entries (apartment-area mean equals median 82.35; D_carmel median 24,773 exceeds the max 8,967); the text names 'Price per square meter' as a tax predictor not shown in Table 4; the DWH paragraph tests 'NOX exogenous' though the test concerns the tax variable. Treat quantitative detail beyond the headline coefficients with care.
Generative-AI editing is disclosed in the Acknowledgments (ChatGPT, GPT-5.5).

Suggested content: Oklahoma's SQ 847 (legislatively referred by SJR 39, on the 3 November 2026 ballot) would cut the annual cap on growth in fair cash value from 3 to 1.75 per cent for homesteads and agricultural land and from 5 to 4 per cent for other real property from tax year 2027, and would replace the senior freeze with an income-tiered scale (no increase at or below the HUD median income for the county or metro area; 0.35, 0.7, 1.05 and 1.4 per cent for each further 20 per cent of median up to 180 per cent; 1.75 per cent above). The existing Oklahoma cap has the same acquisition-reset structure as Proposition 13 (reset on sale or improvement; SQ 676 of 1996 set 5 per cent, SQ 758 of 2012 set 3 per cent for homesteads and farmland). Contrast: Iowa SF 2472, approved by the Governor 18 May 2026, limits county general, rural-services and city general levies to 102 per cent of the prior year's certified dollars (excluding new construction, improvements and boundary changes) from fiscal 2027-28, with the old fixed rate caps resuming as a ceiling from 1 July 2030, and applies the same 102 per cent rule to other rate-limited levies (new Iowa Code 444.25). Attribute the judgement that a levy limit is the 'neutral' option to the Tax Foundation as Tier 2 origin only (one clause). Do NOT write an outcome: the vote is 3 Nov 2026; phrase with 'would' and revisit after the count; the post-vote events/2026-property-tax-revolt-wave.md page (BACKLOG lines 99 and 114) should carry results and the roster. If T1 prefers not to publish a pending-vote sentence, DEFER to that page: all primaries are saved for it. Also correct: the queue note says 12 November; the vote date is 3 November 2026.

Gane is in the Journal of Classical Sociology and already on concepts/technofeudalism.md; the Finance and Society article in the report's reference [10] is by Joel Z. Garrod (the report gives no authors) and is new to the wiki. The report lists Gane and Garrod in references [9] and [10] but cites neither in the body (body cites [1]-[8]).

Author/outlet tiering: Marginal Thinking / LOGV Research is an independent market-research outlet; the author page gives a publications count and an outlet e-mail but no academic post, degree or affiliation. Judged Tier 3 for any claim; not citable as support; not in sources/audit/people-tiers.json.
The report's OECD figure (AI 61 per cent of venture capital in 2025, 30 per cent in 2022) could not be checked: the OECD page returned 403 to ordinary requests. Not recommended for the wiki.

Biglaiser et al.: the TSE publication page returned a bot-verification page; the PDF was reached at the URL the search tool reported (https://www.tse-fr.eu/sites/default/files/TSE/documents/doc/wp/2026/wp_tse_1756.pdf), served openly. A working paper, so results may change; its introduction's market-share and fee-multiple statements come from Statista and Ofcom (2023) footnotes, not the authors' estimates. Microsoft funding is disclosed.

Garrod is a theoretical sociology piece on blockchain; its bearing on rent is thin (rent appears only in a few passing sentences). It merits a short paragraph on the technofeudalism page only, not data-rents.md or the Georgist rent-frontier portal.
